prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map captures the enclosed front cabin of a car from the front-right passenger seat, clearly separating the overhead headliner and flipped-down passenger sun visor (brightest shades at 0.15 to 0.4 m, well within the camera wearer's arm's reach) from the central rearview mirror and left-side steering wheel (medium grey at 0.5 to 0.8 m). Across the five frames, the brightest near-field region shifts as the camera wearer turns their head upward toward the roof in frames 2 and 3 (pushing the sun visor to the lower-left and lower-right edges), faces the visor directly at 0.3 m in frames 1 and 4, and reaches up with their right arm at the right edge in frame 5 to fold the visor against the ceiling while the driver appears at the far-left edge about 0.6 to 0.8 m away facing forward toward the windshield. Compared to the overexposed RGB windshield, the depth map more clearly delineates the 3D layering between the foreground visor, the mid-ground rearview mirror to its left, and the driver's torso and steering wheel below and to the left. However, the depth map is unreliable on transparent and reflective surfaces: it treats the camera wearer's reflected face inside the vanity mirror (which faces and looks back at the camera in frames 1, 2, and 4) as a flat surface at the visor's 0.3 m plane, and collapses the entire exterior scene of parked cars several metres away through the windows into uniform black.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map labels almost the entire interior cabin—including the overhead roof, sun visor, dashboard, and windshield—as a single overarching 'car' instance within 0.2 to 1.0 m of the camera wearer, while sporadically detecting external vehicles and internal reflections across the five frames. In frames 1 and 4, it segments the camera wearer's reflection inside the vanity mirror (0.3 m directly in front and slightly above, facing and looking toward the camera wearer) as a 'person' mask, whereas in frame 2 it picks up three parked cars outside the right passenger window roughly 3 to 8 m away and 1 to 2 m apart from each other, and one exterior car to the far left in frame 4. When the camera wearer's head tilts steeply into the shadowy ceiling in frame 3, the segmentation fails completely (rendering entirely black), and in frame 5 it detects the camera wearer's raised right arm at the right edge (0.2 to 0.3 m away, within arm's reach of the visor) as a 'person' while completely missing the partially occluded driver seated 0.6 to 0.8 m to the left behind the steering wheel. While the map helps isolate distant exterior cars in frame 2 that blend into the bright snow in RGB, it is highly unreliable when it misclassifies the glowing right vanity mirror light and the bottom-right side mirror in frame 4 as 'cell phone' instances and merges distinct interior structures into one mask.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is mostly empty across the sequence, rendering yellow body keypoints only in frames 1 and 4 and detecting no magenta hand skeletons in any frame. In both frames 1 and 4, the estimator places a fragmented yellow upper-body skeleton over the vanity mirror of the passenger sun visor about 0.3 m directly in front of the camera wearer (within arm's reach), where the camera wearer's reflected head and shoulders face and look straight back toward the lens, tightly cropped and occluded by the mirror frame. As the camera wearer turns their head away toward the ceiling in frames 2 and 3 and flips the visor up in frame 5, all pose detections disappear entirely, failing to track the partially visible reflection at the bottom edges of frames 2 and 3, the camera wearer's raised right arm at the right edge of frame 5 (0.2 to 0.3 m away), or the driver seated 0.6 to 0.8 m to the left facing forward with hands near the steering wheel. Rather than revealing hidden posture beyond the RGB image, the pose map is largely unreliable here because it hallucinates a sideways torso configuration from the rectangular edges of the vanity mirror lights while missing real limbs and hands in the cabin.
